summary: Gavin Baker notes that for the first time OpenAI failed to release a model decisively better than rivals on all benchmarks, suggesting potential talent loss is weighing on progress, though OpenAI remains highly valuable due to superior product and massive user distribution.
quote: this is the first time that OpenAI has not been able to clearly beat a competitor on all metrics, you know, a month after a new frontier model was kind of released from one of their chief rivals.

summary: Friedberg argues GPT-5's key upgrade is its auto-routing UX that selects the right underlying model, which gives OpenAI a real product advantage as AI becomes more broadly adopted.
quote: I think from a product experience point of view, this was actually a pretty big upgrade for ChatGPT, and it'll give them a real advantage as people start to access it.

summary: Gavin Baker, a disclosed shareholder of xAI, argues Grok 4 made exceptional benchmark progress and xAI's possession of the largest Blackwell cluster makes him optimistic for Grok 5's competitive position.
quote: I should note my firm is a shareholder of xAI. So as much as I try to be objective, I am for sure biased... they have the largest Blackwell cluster, so I'm optimistic for GROK5.

summary: Gavin Baker cites Meta's significantly revenue-beat quarter as evidence that AI investments are generating real economic returns, driven by AI keeping users engaged longer and improving ad targeting ROAS.

summary: Gavin Baker notes that even Microsoft, whose Copilot product he views as suboptimal, reported astonishing Copilot uptake stats, suggesting AI investments are generating real economic returns across the industry.
quote: even Microsoft. I mean, for me, Copilot is not the best product, but even Microsoft on their call talked, they shared some pretty astonishing stats about Copilot uptake.

summary: Friedberg pushes back on Apple bear narratives, noting that every Apple product cycle has faced similar criticism and Apple has a system built unlike any other in corporate history that should not be counted out.
quote: Rumors of Apple's demise are 30 years old, okay? This is every year the same story. Lack of innovation, copycatting... I would not count Apple out. There's a system there that's built unlike any other in corporate history.
